subject: password expiry and data breaches
title: What If You Never Changed Your Password?

scenes.text: What if you never changed your password? Security experts now say that might be fine.
Offices once forced new passwords every few months, so people picked near-copies of the old one, or wrote them down.
In twenty sixteen, Britain's national cyber security centre said forcing regular changes leaves accounts less safe, not more.
Today America's standards agency, NIST, says websites must not make you change passwords on a schedule.
The catch: if a site leaks it, you must change it. Data breaches have already exposed billions of accounts.
So the real danger was never an old password. It's the same password on every site, where one leak unlocks everything.

description:
What if you never changed your password? In 2016 the UK's National Cyber Security Centre advised organisations not to force regular password expiry, because forced changes lead to predictable new passwords that are more likely to be written down.
NIST's digital identity guidelines now say services shall not require periodic password changes, but shall force a change when there is evidence of compromise.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Be honest: how old is your oldest password? What tech habit should we run through next?
